headline: High-risk default interaction: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths between next-ai-draw-io and xonsh.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and diagrams via MCP/browser-assisted workflows, while xonsh can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands. A shared workspace makes attacker-controlled document content a plausible instruction channel into xonsh. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF xonsh consumes files produced or modified by next-ai-draw-io without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic shell execution from generated content
Add a manual review step before xonsh reads agent_a outputs
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACLs between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and broad network egress, and xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables. If they share a workspace or environment, sensitive documents or secrets touched by agent_a can be exposed to agent_b and then transmitted outward by either agent. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF agent_a stores API keys or document extracts in shared files
IF agent_b is launched with access to the same environment variables or workspace
mitigations: Mount read-only input directories for xonsh
Restrict outbound network for one agent
requires-engineering: isolate per-agent credentials and workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can run multiple instances and use MCP/browser/networked APIs, while xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. On a shared directory, concurrent edits can collide and corrupt diagrams, configs, or generated artifacts. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF either agent edits the same diagram or config file concurrently
mitigations: Serialize writes with a manual queue
Use file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations and natural-language commands, and xonsh can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If xonsh treats agent_a output as authoritative, a mistaken diagram, command, or extracted fact can cascade into real shell actions. The downstream authority in agent_b makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands derived from next-ai-draw-io output
IF there is no verification step before shell execution
mitigations: requires-engineering: add policy checks before shell invocation

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and broad egress, while xonsh touches filesystem contents, configuration, and environment variables. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed in the shared environment, differing retention or residency controls can create a compliance gap. The profiles do not document matching controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the shared workspace
IF retention, residency, or logging policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPAs
